relevance_reason: Reports two unrelated infertile Chinese women with biallelic MEI1 variants, abnormal fertilization with multiple pronuclei and embryonic developmental arrest, along with functional and embryo genomic and transcriptomic studies.

findings.statement: Jiao et al. (2025) described a 32-year-old Chinese woman (F1_II:4) with a 4-year history of primary infertility, regular menses and normal ovarian reserve. Her husband's semen and both partners' karyotypes were normal. Of 22 mature oocytes, the 8 fertilized by ICSI became 3PN or PPN embryos. With conventional IVF, 5 oocytes formed normal 2PN embryos and 3 became 3PN/PPN embryos. All 2PN-derived embryos failed to form blastocysts, whereas 2 of 3 3PN/PPN-derived embryos from ICSI developed into late-stage blastocysts.
quotes: The proband in family 1 (F1_II:4) was a 32-year-old woman with a 4-year history of primary infertility and no prior pregnancies. She had regular menstrual cycles and a normal ovarian reserve.
Among ICSI-fertilized oocytes, eight developed into3PN or PPN embryos. Among IVF-fertilized oocytes, five exhibited normal 2PN formation, while three developed into 3PN/PPN embryos (Fig. 1A).

All 2PN-derived embryos from conventional IVF failed to form blastocysts, and no viable embryos were frozen or implanted. In contrast, two out of three 3PN/PPN-derived embryos from ICSI developed into late-stage blastocysts (Table 1).

phenotypes.hpo_label: Formation of multiple pronuclei during fertilization

findings.statement: Jiao et al. (2025) described a 35-year-old Chinese woman (F2_II:2) with an 8-year history of primary infertility, regular menses, normal ovarian function and patent fallopian tubes. She had 2 unsuccessful IVF cycles and then 1 ICSI cycle. In the ICSI cycle, 3 oocytes formed 2PN embryos and 1 formed a 1PN embryo. All embryos failed to form blastocysts, and transfer of 2 frozen embryos did not result in pregnancy.
quotes: The proband in family 2 (F2_II:2) was a 35-year-old woman presented with an 8-year history of primary infertility. She had regular menstrual cycles and normal ovarian function.
Among these oocytes, three developed into normal 2PN embryos, while one was classified as a one-pronuclear (1PN) embryo (Fig. 3A; Table 1).
All embryos failed to form blastocysts. Viable frozen embryos were implanted but failed to result in pregnancy.

findings.statement: Jiao et al. (2025) performed whole-exome sequencing in 20 women who had a high rate of abnormal fertilization during ICSI at a center in Guangzhou, China. Biallelic MEI1 variants were found in 2 of the 20 women, and all 4 variants were novel.
quotes: Among these 20 patients, MEI1 variants were identified in two infertile women (F1_II:4 and F2_II:2).
WES identified four novel MEI1 variants in both probands.

findings.statement: In the proband of family 1, Jiao et al. (2025) identified compound heterozygous MEI1 variants by whole-exome sequencing, confirmed by Sanger sequencing: c.622T-C (p.Ser208Pro) in exon 6 and c.2647C-T (p.Arg883Ter) in exon 21. The p.Ser208Pro missense variant was absent from gnomAD and was classified as of uncertain significance. In HEK293T cells it did not alter MEI1 protein expression. The p.Arg883Ter nonsense variant had a gnomAD frequency of 6.57E-06. It increased MEI1 mRNA but reduced MEI1 protein levels, which the authors considered consistent with nonsense-mediated decay.
quotes: The proband from family 1 (F1_II:4) carried compound heterozygous variants: c.622T > C (p.Ser208Pro) and c.2647 C > T (p.Arg883Ter) (Fig. 1B; Table 2).

At the protein level, western blot analysis revealed that both p.Arg883Ter variants reduced MEI1 protein abundance (P = 0.031), consistent with nonsense-mediated decay of the truncated transcript (Fig. 3, C-D; Fig. S3).

findings.statement: In the proband of family 2, Jiao et al. (2025) identified compound heterozygous MEI1 variants: a c.3037T-G (p.Trp1013Gly) missense variant in exon 24 and a deletion of exons 21 to 31. The deletion is reported as c.2546_3525del in the text and as c.2546_3825del in the table and discussion. Because the deletion spans c.3037, the patient appeared homozygous for c.3037T-G, and qPCR validated the copy-number loss. The missense variant was absent from gnomAD and increased MEI1 protein levels in HEK293T cells, whereas the deletion did not alter protein expression.
quotes: The proband from family 2 (F2_II:2) carried a compound heterozygous genotype for c.3037T > G (p.Trp1013Gly) and c.2546_3525del (EX21-31del) variants (Fig. 1B and S1; Table 2).
As a result, the F2_II:2 patient appeared to be homozygous for c.3037T > G variant in WES and Sanger sequencing data (Fig. 3B). qPCR further validated the CNV loss in Exons 21 and 31 (Fig. 1B).
In contrast, p.Trp1013Gly increased protein levels (P = 0.016, Fig. 3, C-D). The p.Ser208Pro and E21_E31del variants did not alter protein expression (Fig. 3, C-D).

findings.statement: Jiao et al. (2025) performed whole-genome sequencing and parental-contamination testing on 3 embryos from the family 1 proband. All 3 embryos were triploid with an excess of maternal chromosomes, including an embryo that had appeared to be a normal 2PN embryo. Haplotype analysis indicated that the triploidy was of meiotic origin: meiosis II errors in the 3PN zygote and meiosis I errors in the 3PN blastocyst and the 2PN blastomere. The authors proposed that the MEI1 variants impair meiosis I through abnormal chromosome synapsis.
quotes: However, qPCT confirmed that all embryos were triploid, with the majority of chromosomes originating from the maternal side (Fig. 4B).

In the 3PN zygote, the region downstream of the centromere on chromosome 22 was classified as an SPH segment, suggesting that the triploidy resulted from meiosis II errors. In contrast, both the 3PN blastocyst and the 2PN blastomere exhibited BPH segments downstream of the centromere, indicating that these two embryos originated from meiosis I errors.
We propose that MEI1 variants impair meiosis I by abnormal chromosome synapsis.

findings.statement: Jiao et al. (2025) performed RNA-seq on 3 day-3 embryos from the family 1 proband and compared them with control embryos. They found 2,005 downregulated and 1,904 upregulated genes. Downregulated genes were enriched for meiotic cell cycle and epigenetic regulators, including histone demethylases and deacetylases. Maternal-effect genes were dysregulated, and qPCR confirmed reduced MEI1, MKI67, ASTL and WEE2 expression. The authors suggested a dual mechanism of impaired meiotic and mitotic cell cycles and genomic stability, together with dysregulated epigenetic processes that disrupt zygotic genome activation.
quotes: We identified 2,005 downregulated genes and 1,904 upregulated genes in patient’s embryos (Fig. 8C; Table S3).
The qPCR results confirmed significantly reduced mRNA levels of MEI1 (P = 0.0011), MKI67 (P = 0.0440), ASTL (P = 0.0050), and WEE2 (P = 0.043) in the mutation group compared with controls (Fig. 5G).
Second, MEI1 variants dysregulate epigenetic processes, thereby disrupting zygotic genome activation.

findings.statement: Jiao et al. (2025) summarized reported MEI1 variants and observed that those associated with nonobstructive azoospermia tended to lie toward the N terminus, whereas variants associated with embryonic developmental arrest tended to cluster toward the C terminus. They stated that this hypothesis requires further validation.
quotes: Interestingly, NOA-associated variants tend to locate towards the N-terminal, while EDA-related variants - including three novel variants identified in our study – tends to cluster toward the C-terminal.

findings.statement: Jiao et al. (2025) recommended screening for MEI1 variants in patients with abnormal fertilization patterns, especially multiple pronuclei after ICSI. They noted that even 2PN embryos that look morphologically normal may be triploid. They also suggested that 3PN/PPN blastocysts might implant and could develop into hydatidiform moles in natural pregnancies.
quotes: For clinical practice, we recommend MEI1 variant screening in patients showing abnormal fertilization patterns, especially multiple pronuclei following ICSI.
Notably, these 3PN/PPN embryos successfully developed to blastocyst stage, suggesting they could implant and potentially develop into hydatidiform moles in natural pregnancies.

relevance_reason: Reports biallelic MEI1 variants in two unrelated families with female infertility due to early embryonic arrest and implantation failure (OZEMA26), with functional studies.

findings.statement: Chen et al. (2026) studied female patients with primary infertility characterized by early embryonic arrest (EEA) and implantation failure, including affected women from 2 unrelated families carrying biallelic MEI1 variants.
quotes: Female patients with primary infertility characterized by EEA and implantation failure were recruited, and peripheral blood samples were collected.
We identified a novel homozygous variant and a compound heterozygous variant in MEI1 from two unrelated families.

findings.statement: In affected women from 2 unrelated families with female infertility due to early embryonic arrest and implantation failure, Chen et al. (2026) identified biallelic MEI1 variants by whole-exome sequencing, confirmed by Sanger sequencing: a novel homozygous variant in one family and compound heterozygous variants in the other. Bioinformatics analysis indicated the variants were rare and possibly deleterious.
quotes: Whole-exome sequencing was performed, and the identified variants were confirmed by Sanger sequencing.
We identified a novel homozygous variant and a compound heterozygous variant in MEI1 from two unrelated families.
Analysis using multiple bioinformatics tools revealed that these variants are rare and may be deleterious.

findings.statement: In HEK293T cells transfected with wildtype and mutant constructs, Chen et al. (2026) found that the MEI1 variants did not alter the subcellular localization of MEI1 but significantly affected its mRNA and protein expression levels, potentially leading to impaired protein function.
quotes: In vitro experiments revealed that these mutations do not alter the subcellular localization of MEI1 but significantly affect its mRNA and protein expression levels, potentially leading to impaired protein function.

relevance_reason: Reports a consanguineous family with a homozygous MEI1 exon 19 deletion, in which a female patient had embryonic arrest (OZEMA26) and her brother had azoospermia. The paper includes functional and embryo aneuploidy data.

findings.statement: Liu et al. (2025) studied a consanguineous family with an infertile female patient whose embryos arrested and an infertile male patient with azoospermia. Preimplantation genetic testing showed high rates of chromosomal abnormalities in the arrested embryos.
quotes: This study characterized a male infertile patient suffering from azoospermia and a female infertile patient with embryonic arrest from one consanguineous family.
Highly chromosomal anomalies were revealed in arrested embryos with MEI1 mutation.

findings.statement: In the 2 affected members of a consanguineous family, a woman with embryonic arrest and a man with azoospermia, Liu et al. (2025) found a homozygous deletion of all of exon 19 of the MEI1 gene. They identified it by whole-exome sequencing and confirmed it by Sanger sequencing. cDNA sequencing confirmed that the exon was missing from the transcript, and quantitative expression analysis found almost no MEI1 exon 19 expression in the patients. The patients' mother was a heterozygous carrier. In transfected HEK293T cells, Western blotting showed a truncated MEI1 protein, consistent with the predicted premature termination in exon 20.
quotes: The novel homozygous whole exon deletion of exon 19 in MEI1 was detected by WES.
Quantitative expression revealed that the deletion result in almost no detectable expression of MEI1 Exon 19 in patients, and their mother is a heterozygous carrier of this whole exon deletion.
Western blotting revealed that the whole exon deletion in MEI1 result in production of truncated MEI1 protein, corresponding to the predicted premature termination at Exon 20 of MEI1.

variants.as_reported: homozygous whole exon deletion of exon 19

findings.statement: Liu et al. (2025) suggested that aneuploidy in embryos carrying the MEI1 mutation may explain their reduced developmental potential and their arrest.
quotes: also revealed the aneuploidies of embryos with MEI1 mutation as a potential reason for declined developmental potency and embryonic arrest.

relevance_reason: Case report of an infertile female with embryonic arrest and recurrent implantation failure who carried compound heterozygous MEI1 frameshift variants, with analysis of her embryos.

findings.statement: Wu et al. (2024) reported a female infertile patient with embryonic arrest and recurrent implantation failure.
quotes: This study presents a case of a female infertile patient suffering from embryonic arrest and recurrent implantation failure.

findings.statement: In a female patient with embryonic arrest and recurrent implantation failure, Wu et al. (2024) used whole-exome sequencing, with Sanger sequencing confirmation, to identify compound heterozygous frameshift variants in the MEI1 gene (NM_152513.3): c.3002delC and c.2264_2268+11delGTGAGGTATGGACCAC. Each variant was inherited from a heterozygous parent, consistent with autosomal recessive inheritance.
quotes: We identified two novel pathogenic frameshift variants in the MEI1 gene (NM_152513.3, c.3002delC, c.2264_2268 + 11delGTGAGGTATGGACCAC) in the proband.
These two variants were inherited from her heterozygous parents, consistent with autosomal recessive genetic transmission.

findings.statement: Wu et al. (2024) found that 2 day-3 cleavage-stage embryos and 2 day-6 blastocysts from the MEI1-mutant patient were all aneuploid, with numerous monosomies and trisomies, on whole-genome sequencing and whole-genome bisulfite sequencing. Global methylation levels in the 2 blastocysts were 0.344 and 0.168, far outside the optimal window of 0.25 to 0.27. The authors suggested that the genetic makeup of arrested embryos may help explain why MEI1 mutations cause either embryonic arrest or monospermic androgenetic hydatidiform moles.
quotes: Notably, two Day 3 embryos and two Day 6 blastocysts were all aneuploid, with numerous monosomy and trisomy events.
Moreover, global methylation levels greatly deviated from the optimized window of 0.25-0.27, measuring 0.344 and 0.168 for the respective blastocysts.
the genetic makeup of the arrested embryos of MEI1 patients provides important clues for understanding the different disease mechanisms of the two phenotypes

relevance_reason: Reports biallelic MEI1 mutations in women with recurrent hydatidiform moles, early embryonic arrest, and recurrent implantation failure. This is the defining phenotype of OZEMA26.

findings.statement: Dong et al. (2021) studied 9 women with primary infertility from 7 independent families. The first was a pedigree in which 2 sisters had recurrent hydatidiform moles. The other 7 patients from 6 families had embryonic arrest or recurrent implantation failure, found by screening patients with embryonic arrest, recurrent implantation failure, or recurrent pregnancy loss.
quotes: We first focused on a pedigree in which two sisters were diagnosed with recurrent hydatidiform moles in December 2018.
we identified five novel mutations in MEI1 in nine patients from seven independent families.
Apart from recurrent hydatidiform moles, biallelic mutations in MEI1 were also associated with early embryonic arrest and recurrent implantation failure.

findings.statement: Dong et al. (2021) used whole-exome sequencing, with confirmation by Sanger sequencing, to identify 5 novel biallelic MEI1 mutations in 9 infertile women from 7 families. Two novel mutations were found in the pedigree with 2 sisters who had recurrent hydatidiform moles. Three further novel mutations were found in 7 patients from 6 families with embryonic arrest or recurrent implantation failure.
quotes: After genetic analysis, two novel mutations in MEI1 were identified.
found another three novel MEI1 mutations in seven new patients from six families recruited from December 2018 to May 2020.
The MEI1 mutations were screened using whole-exome sequencing and were confirmed by the Sanger sequencing.

findings.statement: In in vitro studies by Dong et al. (2021), protein-truncating and missense MEI1 mutations reduced MEI1 protein levels on western blot. In minigene assays, splicing mutations caused abnormal alternative splicing of MEI1.
quotes: we demonstrated that protein-truncating and missense mutations reduced the protein level of MEI1, while the splicing mutations caused abnormal alternative splicing of MEI1.
